Date range picker: a clearer custom range and a shorter Absolute tab

The owner asked (2026-11-18): make Custom range stand out instead of reading like one more quick range, and make the Absolute tab much shorter, after checking how other products do it. These are screenshots of the real component on branch proposal/date-picker-compact, dark theme, 1280 × 720 laptop and 390 px phone. Each option is a working example in the docs (/components/date-range-picker, the Proposal… examples), so you can click it. Today's behaviour is unchanged until you pick. Decision RV-P2-1.

Inline custom range + fields beside the calendar

Custom range: show the Duration and Unit on one line under the quick ranges (option Inline). It is visible without a click, needs no second screen and no Back button, and it doubles as an editor: pick Last 7 days, change 7 to 10. Kibana does exactly this; Grafana, Sentry and Datadog reach the same goal with a typed field.

Absolute: put the Start and End fields beside the calendar on a laptop (option C, side by side). The panel drops from 664 px to 398 px tall (−40 %) and the calendar stays in view, so a mouse user still clicks two days; it is the layout Cloudscape (AWS) and Supabase use. On a phone it stacks. The calendar keeps only the weeks the month needs, End at now becomes a checkbox, and Refresh every moves into the footer next to Cancel and Apply.

If you would rather keep the panel narrow, pick A, compact (535 px, −19 %). If your people mostly type dates, B, fields first is the shortest (252 px) but hides the calendar behind a click.

1 · Custom range: make it stand out

Today Custom range › is a row styled exactly like the quick ranges, so it reads as one more choice. Two alternatives, both built:

What opens after the click (Today and Link)

Link

The quick ranges end at a divider and Custom range is a link-variant Button with a sliders icon; the custom duration in use is printed beside it.

  • Pro: no height cost, clearly a different kind of action.
  • Con: still a second screen and a Back button; two clicks to a custom value.
  • A11y: a real button, Tab-reachable after the quick-range radios; focus moves into Duration and back.

Inline ★

A Custom range group (a fieldset named by its legend) with Duration and Unit on one line. Picking a quick range fills it in; typing a number or picking a unit selects it (check mark beside the heading).

  • Pro: visible at once, no second screen, edits a quick range in place. Kibana's pattern.
  • Con: +47 px on the Relative tab (won back by moving Refresh every to the footer).
  • A11y: labelled fields (Duration, Unit) inside a named group; tabbing through does not change the selection, only typing or choosing does.

A third tab (not built)

Relative · Custom · Absolute. Rejected: Custom is a relative range, so it would split one idea over two tabs, and three tabs in a 276 px panel get cramped (Cloudscape keeps custom inside its Relative mode).

Phone 390 px

2 · Absolute: three shorter layouts

What the three share: the calendar shows only the weeks the month needs (most months 5 rows instead of 6, about 40 px saved), and Refresh every moves from its own row into the footer as a small ↻ 5 min select beside Cancel and Apply (about 50 px saved, on both tabs). Grafana and Kibana 9.5 likewise keep auto-refresh out of the range form.

A · Compact

Calendar first as today; each label sits before its date and time on one line; End at now is a checkbox.

  • Pro: same narrow 276 px panel and the same reading order as today; fits a 720 px screen.
  • Con: only −19 %; still a tall panel.
  • A11y: unchanged order (grid, Start, End, End at now, footer); labels still bound to their inputs.

B · Fields first

Start and End rows first, then End at now and a Choose date link that opens the calendar below (Grafana's From/To, Kibana's per-end popovers).

  • Pro: by far the shortest; typing a known range is fastest.
  • Con: a mouse user needs one more click to see a calendar; picking by eye is the common case in an investigation.
  • A11y: Choose date is a disclosure button (aria-expanded, aria-controls the calendar); focus stays on it, the calendar follows in Tab order.

C · Side by side ★

From 640 px the fields column sits beside the calendar; both tabs share the width, and the quick ranges read in three columns.

  • Pro: short and the calendar is always visible; Cloudscape (AWS), Supabase and Grafana use a wide panel on desktop.
  • Con: 534 px wide instead of 276 px; needs room beside the trigger (it flips and is capped at the screen width).
  • A11y: DOM order is calendar then fields, which is also the visual order left to right (mirrored in right-to-left).

Takeaways

  • Custom relative is inline almost everywhere (Kibana's field, or a typed value in Grafana, Sentry, Datadog). Only Cloudscape hides it behind a radio, and even it shows the fields in place, never on a second screen.
  • Short absolute panels either show the calendar on demand (Grafana, Kibana) or go wide (Cloudscape, Supabase) — never a tall single column with everything.
  • Auto-refresh lives outside the range form (Grafana, Kibana 9.5, the live toggles of Vercel, Supabase, Datadog). Moving it to the footer is the small step; a separate control beside the trigger is the bigger one, left for later.
  • “Now” is a value of the end (Grafana's now, Kibana's Now tab), which matches a small End at now checkbox next to the end fields.

How to try them and decide

  • Docs page /components/date-range-picker, examples ProposalCustomLink, ProposalCustomInline, ProposalAbsoluteCompact, ProposalAbsoluteFieldsFirst, ProposalAbsoluteSideBySide and ProposalRecommended.
  • They are two temporary props: custom-range-display="row | link | inline" and absolute-layout="stacked | compact | fields-first | side-by-side". Their defaults keep today's panel.
  • Reply with one choice for each (for example “inline + side by side”). The chosen ones become the only behaviour, and the two props and the other examples are removed before the merge.
